title: Product PRD & Release Notes: Unified Inference v18 — Overview, Roadmap, Pricing, Design Specs
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary

This document consolidates the product overview, PRD highlights, high-level design specs, roadmap and themes, pricing & packaging notes, and release notes for Unified Inference v18 (UI v18). UI v18 continues Redwood’s mission to provide a single, predictable inference runtime across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments with improved cost controls, routing intelligence, and observability.

Goals (Q1–Q2 2027)
- Improve tail-latency and predictable p95/P99 latency for generation workloads by 15% on average.
- Reduce per-token inference cost by 10% for common web-scale workloads via smarter routing, dynamic quantization, and cache-aware batching.
- Launch a simplified pricing tier for committed throughput customers and a developer-friendly freemium experimentation tier.
- Ship first-class rollout automation for model variant canaries and automated fallback to cheaper model variants under capacity pressure.

1) Product overview (one-paragraph)
UI v18 extends the Unified Inference product line by adding adaptive model routing, dynamic quantization profiles per workload, and integrated cost-visibility for per-request routing decisions. The release targets both PLG developer velocity improvements (self-serve tiers, SDK helpers, quickstart prompts) and enterprise features (committed throughput SKUs, expanded Private deployment telemetry).

2) PRD: Key requirements (must-have)
- Functional
  1. Adaptive routing engine that routes requests by policy: latency-first, cost-first, region-aware, and SLO-preserving.
  2. Dynamic quantization profiles (0/4/8-bit) selectable per model variant and per-customer workload signature.
  3. Per-request cost estimate and post-hoc token-cost breakdown surfaced in Console and API.
  4. Canary and automated fallback rollout mechanism tied to quality and latency monitors.
  5. Developer SDK helpers for common patterns (chat with streaming, function-calls, embeddings) and one-line quickstarts.
- Non-functional
  - SLOs: 99.95% availability for Hosted endpoints; p95 latency targets defined per model-class (see table below).
  - Scale: Support 3x current peak requests per second in Dedicated pools with horizontal autoscaling.
  - Security: Support KMS keys in Private deployments and audit-log events for all routing decisions.

Acceptance criteria (examples)
- Routing engine demonstrates 10% average token-cost reduction on the standard benchmark suite without increasing customer-observed p95 by >5%.
- Dynamic quantization has automated compatibility checks and an opt-out flag; 95% of customer workloads pass compatibility check with no fallback.
- Console shows per-request cost estimate within ±15% of billed unit cost for >99% of sampled requests.

3) Design specs (high level)
- Architecture overview:
  - New component: Routing Orchestrator service (stateless control plane) that computes route decisions and writes policy traces to the Trace Store.
  - Execution path: API Gateway -> AuthN/AuthZ -> Routing Orchestrator -> Model Serving Cluster (selected model variant) -> Response and Cost Telemetry emitted.
  - Persistence: Route policies stored in Config Service with versioned policy objects and simple rollback APIs.

- Data contract & telemetry:
  - RouteDecision proto fields (for trace): request_id, customer_id, model_id, variant_id, policy_reason, estimated_cost_usd, trace_latency_ms.
  - Auditing: every Routing decision must emit an audit event to Audit Log stream (for compliance).

- Compatibility and safety:
  - Quality gate (pre-rollout): run 1000 synthetic prompts and 5 customer prompt-sets; require BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity thresholds defined per model.
  - Fallback policy: if quality/regression detected, automatically revert active percentage by 50% and notify owners.

- Table: p95 latency targets (example)
  | Model class | Typical seq len | p95 latency target (ms) | Notes |
  | small-encoder | 32 | 80 | embeddings/short-completions |
  | med-encoder-decoder | 128 | 180 | chat workloads |
  | large-decoder | 512 | 350 | long-form generation |

4) Roadmap & themes (next 6 months)
- Theme A: Cost-aware routing & autoscaling (owner: Eng - Serving Runtime)
  - M1 (Mar 2027): Routing Orchestrator spike and policy DSL v0.1.
  - M2 (Apr 2027): Integrate cost model and confidence signals; console UX for route policy creation.
  - M3 (May 2027): Beta with 10 pilot customers for Dedicated and Hosted.
- Theme B: Developer velocity & SDKs (owner: Eng - Developer Experience)
  - M1: Quickstart templates for chat, function-calls, and embeddings; 1-click deploy.
  - M2: Streaming SDK improvements and client-side cost estimator.
- Theme C: Enterprise packaging & Private deployment observability (owner: Product + Eng Private Deployments)
  - M1: Committed Throughput SKU pricing, contract template for Reserved Capacity.
  - M2: Expanded audit and telemetry export (Syslog, Splunk, S3).

5) Pricing & packaging notes
- New SKUs introduced in UI v18:
  - Freemium Developer Tier: 100k tokens/month free for new accounts; soft rate limits for experimentation.
  - Pay-as-you-go Hosted: unchanged base per-token rates; improved visibility reduces cost via recommendations.
  - Committed Throughput (Reserved Capacity): monthly committed-QPS pricing with 20% discount vs PAYG for 6-month commit, 28% for 12-month commit.
  - Enterprise: Private deployment license is unchanged but now includes a telemetry export add-on and extended retention as a paid add-on.

- Pricing examples (illustrative):
  - PAYG small-gen model: $0.002 per 1k tokens (no change)
  - Committed Throughput 6mo: effective $0.0016 per 1k tokens (20% discount)
  - Committed Throughput 12mo: effective $0.00144 per 1k tokens (28% discount)

- Billing & metering changes:
  - Introduce per-route billing labels so customers can split billing by feature.
  - Add committed-throughput credits consumption model in billing exports (CSV/Parquet).

6) Release notes (UI v18 GA — 2027-03-01)
- Highlights:
  - Adaptive Routing Orchestrator (GA) — routes by latency/cost/region/SLOs; supports Canary rollouts and automated fallback.
  - Dynamic Quantization Profiles — per-variant quantization with automated compatibility checks and rollback.
  - Committed Throughput SKU — Reserved Capacity ordering via Console with contract templates.
  - Cost Visibility — per-request cost estimates and token-level cost breakdowns in Console/Exports.
  - SDK updates — streaming stability improvements and one-line quickstart templates.

- Breaking changes / Migration notes:
  1. Billing export schema change: new columns route_label, estimated_cost_usd — customers using billing parsers must update.
  2. API minor change: /v1/requests now returns route_decision metadata when requested (opt-in via ?include_route=true). Update client SDKs to handle additional fields.

- Rollout plan:
  1. Internal dogfood (2 weeks): Deploy to staging and Redwood internal traffic; exercise Dedicated pools and Private deployment smoke tests.
  2. Beta (4 weeks): Invite 10 pilot customers across Hosted and Dedicated. Active SRE on-call and 24/7 paging for first 72 hours of beta.
  3. Gradual GA (2 weeks): 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% traffic ramp with automatic quality checks and manual approval gates at each step.

- Post-release monitoring checklist:
  - Route decisions: percent routed to new variants, average estimated_cost_usd delta vs baseline.
  - Latency and error budget burn by model-class and region.
  - Billing drift: reconcile estimated_cost_usd vs billed amounts for sample window.

7) Ownership & contacts
- Product lead: Aisha Patel (product) — roadmap, pricing, customer outreach.
- Eng lead (Serving runtime): Marcus Lee (engineering) — routing orchestrator, quantization, perf work.
- Eng lead (DX): Sofia Müller (developer-experience) — SDKs, quickstarts, developer docs.
- SRE lead: Diego Ramos (eng-sre) — rollout/runbook, incident response.

8) Runbooks & playbooks (summary)
- Canary failure playbook (short):
  1. Detect: quality/regression alert fires (automated).
  2. Contain: rollback to previous policy/variant and reduce traffic to fallback by 75%.
  3. Mitigate: apply hotfix or disable routing policy; notify owners and customers.
  4. Postmortem: 72-hour postmortem with RCA, mitigations, and compensating controls.

- Billing discrepancy playbook (short):
  1. Triage: compare estimated_cost_usd vs billed for sample; check metering logs for missing labels.
  2. Correct: issue invoice credit if tracking error >5% for customer and patch metering pipeline.

Attachments & references
- Related product pages: see related_pages.
- Design artifacts: routing-orchestrator-sequence-diagram.vsdx, dynamic-quantization-profile.json (stored in Design repo).

Appendix: Example route policy (DSL v0.1)
1. name: low-cost-chat
2. match: model.family == "chat" && request.latency_slo_ms >= 150
3. decision: prefer variant.quantized if estimated_cost_usd < threshold && quality_risk_score < 0.2
4. fallback: revert to variant.base on quality regression

Notes and open questions
- Quality risk scoring: define and operationalize a robust method that correlates with customer satisfaction; current approach uses embedding-similarity and token-delta heuristics.
- Pricing elasticity: monitor adoption of Committed Throughput SKU; adjust discounts if onboarding rate < 15% of enterprise customers in first 6 months.
